title: Google confirmed as company behind proposed Roanoke County data center
key_facts: The Western Virginia Regional Industrial Facility Authority (WVRIFA) confirmed on Friday 16 Oct 2026 that Google is the company evaluating Wood Haven Technology Park for a potential data centre (WDBJ7).
The 94-acre site at the Interstate 81/581 junction is jointly owned by Roanoke, Roanoke County and Salem; Google is operating as Clearview Dynamics.
Google is in a due diligence and inspection period expected to run through March 2027, covering engineering and geotechnical assessments, utility capacity studies and environmental reviews.
Roanoke County Administrator Richard Caywood said it would be 'the largest industrial project in the county's history'.
The site, about 14 miles from Google's Botetourt County campus announced last year, would use Spring Hollow Reservoir as its water source.
Google's Clay Allsop, regional public affairs manager, said the company will continue its due diligence and keep the community updated.
quote_evidence: Google is the company evaluating Wood Haven Technology Park for a potential data center, the Western Virginia Regional Industrial Facility Authority (WVRIFA) confirmed Friday.
Google, operating as Clearview Dynamics, is in a due diligence and inspection period expected to run through March 2027.
“At least in order of magnitude this would represent the largest industrial project in the county’s history and at least the Roanoke Valley’s history as well,” Caywood said.
why_it_matters_hint: Google is confirmed as the company behind what local leaders call the largest industrial project in the county's history, but it is still only evaluating the site.
notes: Google is still in due diligence and has not committed to build. The article does not state a project size in megawatts or dollars.
